title: Request Flow & Load Balancing
summary: See how routing, finite workers, and queues combine to determine response time.
outcomes: Separate queue time from service time in an end-to-end request.
Compare round-robin and least-outstanding routing under stated assumptions.
Explain why load balancing cannot create service capacity.

title: Capacity Estimation
summary: Turn product assumptions into transparent ranges for traffic, storage, bandwidth, and concurrent work.
outcomes: Convert daily usage into average and peak request rates with explicit units.
Estimate retained data, response bandwidth, and mean concurrency from stated assumptions.
Explain uncertainty, exclusions, and the difference between an estimate and measured capacity.

title: Distributed Rate Limiter
summary: Control bursts and protect shared capacity while making counter scope, overshoot, and failure policy explicit.
outcomes: Compare fixed-window and token-bucket decisions for the same request schedule.
Explain and calculate overshoot from independent per-node counters.
Choose an enforcement scope and backend-failure policy for a concrete operation.

title: Cache-Aside
summary: Understand cache hits, misses, TTL expiry, stale data, and origin load through a deterministic cache-aside simulation.
outcomes: Trace a GET through cache lookup, origin read, and cache fill with explicit latencies.
Explain why an origin update does not invalidate a cached entry under cache-aside.
Identify stale reads, cold-start bursts, and the effect of cache or origin unavailability.

title: URL Shortener Design Workshop
summary: Build and defend a URL-shortener design across ten draft stages, from requirements and estimates to failures, operations and interview explanations.
outcomes: Separate required behavior from assumptions, non-goals and correctness constraints.
Calculate demand and data growth, then explain how changing one assumption affects the design.
Defend bounded create retries, redirect caching, expiry and error behavior.
Explain permanent code reservations, immutable destinations and the atomic create/replay boundary.
Trace successful creation, active redirect, lost-response recovery and expiry rejection in an illustrative architecture.
Defend cache/eligibility boundaries and diagnose overload, stale mappings and unavailable dependencies.
Define operational signals, preserve guarantees across rollback and explain the design simply with changed-requirement follow-ups.

title: Queues & Tail Latency
summary: Explore finite workers, waiting limits, rejection and slow jobs. Explain queue time and successful latency from an authoritative Java trace.
outcomes: Separate waiting, service and total latency for a completed job.
Compare buffering and worker capacity while reporting rejected and unfinished work.
Explain FIFO waiting and limits using a changed job duration.

title: Delivery, ACKs & Duplicate Work
summary: Trace independent delivery attempts, durable effects and acknowledgments. Explain crash windows, lease expiry and repeated work from Java evidence.
outcomes: Distinguish delivery attempts, durable effects and accepted acknowledgments.
Predict how acknowledgment order, crashes and lost receipts change repeated or missing work.
Explain lease deadlines, stale tokens, dead letters and limited observation without inventing guarantees.
Choose the application boundary that later needs idempotency protection.

title: Data Models & Access Patterns
summary: Choose keys and indexes from the reads you need and the rules writes must preserve. Compare scans, scoped uniqueness and logical maintenance in a small Java model.
outcomes: Turn lookup, range and insert requirements into explicit access patterns.
Compare examined index entries, fetched records and returned records separately.
Distinguish primary identity, scoped business-key uniqueness and index maintenance.
Defend a storage family from queries and invariants while stating unmodeled guarantees.

title: Transactions & Isolation
summary: Inspect reservation races and related writes that commit or abort, using Java snapshots and explicit invariant evidence.
outcomes: Distinguish earlier client observations from current shared stock.
Predict accepted quantities and rejected reservations for an explicit interleaving.
Explain separate nonnegative, capacity and conservation checks.
Defend a current-state acceptance boundary while stating unmodeled transaction guarantees.
Distinguish private preparation from published effects and explain what abort discards.
Use separate conservation, aborted-effect and history checks to defend a related-write boundary.
